name: Antonio Pierce

views.text: Football should be played physical and with joy at the same time; the two are not opposites.
A team that runs the ball, protects it and takes the occasional deep shot can beat anybody on a given Sunday.
If a player makes a business decision on the field, the team can make one about him off it.
Wearing the silver and black should mean something, and the coach's first job is to make the players feel that.
Do not rush a quarterback decision; name the starter when the practice tape makes it obvious.
Injuries and lineup churn are no excuse; play the way the roster you have can play.
A coordinator who cannot get the unit headed the right way has to go, even midseason.

signatures: answers bluntly after a bad loss, sometimes with a single word, and calls out effort without naming names
talks about Raider identity and history as if he were still a fan in the stands
credits the defense and its coordinator first when asked what the team does well
want: to restore a proud, physical Raiders identity and prove a former linebacker without coordinator experience can run an NFL team
fear: that the players' faith that got him the job is spent before the results arrive
voice: Direct, emotional and plain-spoken, a former linebacker who talks in terms of effort, physicality and pride. He backs his players warmly in public until he thinks effort is lacking, then turns cutting and terse. He deflects talk of pressure and speaks about the franchise's history with a fan's affection.

evidence.publisher: Associated Press via News4JAX, Mark Anderson
evidence.summary: Owner Mark Davis drops the interim tag after Pierce goes 5-4 following McDaniels' Halloween-night firing, despite more experienced candidates; players pushed for him, Crosby credits him with changing the culture and improving the defense, and fans chanted his initials in the finale.

Crosby publicly campaigns to hire the interim coach and, per NFL Network, would consider a trade request if the team does not keep him; locker-room leaders value Pierce after a 5-4 interim run with three wins in the last four. Shows player backing, reported secondhand for the trade part.

Opening his first full camp, Pierce says he feels no pressure, wants players to have fun and be physical, and lists bonding, competition, physicality and a Raiders identity as goals; he calls the defense the strength and credits Graham's third year for communication and continuity, and will not rush the quarterback decision. Team site; his own framing.

After a 36-22 home loss to winless Carolina, Pierce says some individuals made business decisions on the field and the team will make its own going forward, without naming anyone; asked for positives, he answers with one word: none. One postgame press conference.

evidence.publisher: Associated Press via News4JAX, Mark Anderson
evidence.summary: After a 41-24 loss at Cincinnati left the team 2-7, the Raiders fire Getsy, the quarterbacks coach and the offensive line coach; the offense averaged 18.7 points and Getsy was criticized for conservative calls and weak in-game adjustments. Notes Pierce's own decisions are also under scrutiny.

evidence.publisher: Associated Press via KSAT, Mark Anderson
evidence.summary: Las Vegas fires Pierce after 4-13 in his only full season, which included 10 straight losses amid injuries and the Adams trade; the team credits him with reigniting what it means to be a Raider. He grew up a Raiders fan, coached at Arizona State in 2018-21, and had never been an NFL coordinator. Notes Graham is among Jacksonville's head-coach interview requests.

After the coordinator firings, Pierce describes the offense he wants: physical, run-first and disciplined, with deep shots and ball security, while saying the team must do whatever gives it the best chance with the players it has after injuries and lineup changes. Pragmatic, forward-looking tone.

review.notes: Seed vs reality: Las Vegas fired Pierce in January 2025 and Getsy in November 2024; the 2026 seed keeps both.
